direction: Rigidity-matrix soft-mode and self-stress surgery: build the contact graph at tolerance $10^{-6}$, parametrise each point by a $6\times5$ tangent basis to get the $\sim560\times580$ rigidity matrix $R$ with rows $(e_i^\top (I-x_ix_i^\top),\, e_j^\top (I-x_jx_j^\top))$ on contacts, compute its SVD (or the LP dual forces from one LP polish), and generate perturbations as random combinations of the 20–40 right singular vectors with smallest singular values, scaled to RMS point displacement 0.05–0.25, optionally plus a component that specifically separates the 5–10 contact pairs carrying the largest dual force; follow each such kick by a feasibility phase minimising $\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t_{\rm target})^2$ with $t_{\rm target}=0.5958$ via Riemannian Adam for 500–1000 steps before switching to ordinary annealed softmax and a short LP polish, accepting a new basin only when its contact graph differs materially (Jaccard $<0.9$) so the solver cannot slide back along the same active set.

idea: Antipodal plus cyclic-shift orbit constrained search with release-perturb-rejam to find a new contact topology
direction: Symmetry-constrained de novo search, ignoring `best.npy`/`record.npy` until a final comparison: first solve the antipodal problem with exactly 58 representatives $y_k$ and points $\pm y_k$, minimising $\max_{k<\ell}|\langle y_k,y_\ell\rangle|$ (softmax over both signs, $\beta:50\to1500$, Adam on the sphere, many random restarts in 5–10s slices), since antipodality halves the degrees of freedom and enforces a balanced contact graph; in parallel try an orbit construction under the order-12 group generated by the 6-cycle coordinate permutation and one coordinate sign flip, choosing generic orbits of size 12 plus smaller special orbits on coordinate axes/equal-coordinate vectors to total exactly 116 and optimising only the orbit representatives; for each constrained optimum, release the constraint, perturb by $10^{-3}$–$10^{-2}$, re-optimise unconstrained with annealed softmax, LP-polish the best two or three released candidates, and keep whichever of the constrained families produces a contact-degree distribution with lower variance than the incumbent's 2–20 spread.

direction: Large spatial-cluster excision and sequential repacking from the incumbent: pick a centre point (alternately a worst hub, a random point, and a point from the PCA projection periphery), delete all 24–36 points within a large cosine cap around it (e.g. $\langle x_i,c\rangle>0.0$, topped up to a fixed count by nearest neighbours), freeze the remaining points, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time, each at the deepest hole found from 20,000–50,000 random candidates against the current set followed by 100 steps of deepest-hole refinement, with a short tangential softmax relaxation (300 steps, $\beta:30\to300$) after every 4–6 insertions; then unfreeze everything, run annealed softmax (800–1200 steps, $\beta:50\to1000$), and LP-polish only if the contact set at tolerance $10^{-7}$ has Jaccard similarity $<0.85$ to the incumbent's or the pre-LP score is within 0.002 of it, cycling through several centres/seeds with an elitist keep-best and a hard internal deadline of 160s reserving 20s for a final LP polish of the overall best.

idea: Second-order active-set descent along the rigidity nullspace of the flat plateau to lower the minimax cosine.
direction: Exploit the floppy modes of the incumbent with second-order active-set descent rather than another random kick: load `best.npy`, collect all pairs with slack below $3\times10^{-7}$, build the rigidity matrix in a $116\times5$ tangent basis, compute its SVD/nullspace, and search nullspace directions for one whose second-order change lowers the largest pair cosines while keeping first-order active cosines unchanged to first order. Take backtracking steps of sizes such as $10^{-2},3\times10^{-3},10^{-3},3\times10^{-4}$ along the best few nullspace directions, renormalize, evaluate the exact maximum, then run a short LP polish; repeat with updated active sets until the 170-second internal deadline. This directly attacks the flat valley visible in the slack plot and should either produce a genuinely lower jammed point or certify that this basin is locally rigid.

idea: Breed diverse Riesz and soft-max basins via Procrustes-Hungarian alignment and hemisphere/half crossover with hole repair
direction: Create genuinely different basins and recombine them genetically instead of perturbing one parent: during the first 90 seconds generate 8–12 diverse local optima from random starts using short Riesz-energy quenches with several exponents $s\in\{1,4,12\}$, soft-max quenches, and one heavily point-deleted/reinserted variant of the incumbent, polishing each only briefly. Align every pair of distinct optima by orthogonal Procrustes rotation and Hungarian point matching, form children by taking complementary hemispheres or matched halves from two parents, delete any child points creating cosines above the parents’ range, refill from the other parent or a deep-hole candidate, then quench and LP-polish the children. Rank parents and children by exact maximum cosine and by contact-graph signature so selection preserves topological diversity, not just near-duplicates of the incumbent.

N-continuation through smaller jammed codes by deleting high-load/random/cap subsets, re-jamming, then greedy deepest-hole reinsertion with short quenches and capped LP polishes.
direction: Use a carefully time-boxed $N$-continuation path that changes the contact topology by construction: delete 12–20 points from the incumbent in several ways—highest near-contact load, random subsets, and one spatial cap—re-jam the resulting 96–104-point codes, then reinsert the missing points one at a time at an approximately deepest spherical hole computed from a few thousand random candidates plus local hole refinement. After each insertion run only a short soft-max quench, with a 1–2 second LP polish every few insertions and a longer final polish reserved for the last 20 seconds; maintain the incumbent throughout and return it if any stage is unfinished. Unlike a single large kick, passing through smaller jammed codes forces deletion and creation of many contacts, while strict per-stage time caps avoid the timeouts and unfinished constructions seen in earlier grow-and-shrink attempts.

idea: Combine isostatic re-jamming with worst-pair geodesic micro-descent and multiplicative hinge quenches plus hub-deletion and subset-rotation basin hops.

Symmetry-constrained global search over antipodal, cyclic-shift-plus-antipode, and signed-permutation lattice-pattern orbits with annealed soft-max Adam on generators then blended symmetry release and free quench plus LP re-jamming.
direction: Run a de novo symmetry-constrained global search, ignoring the record except as a fallback, over several orbit constructions whose sizes sum to 116: 58 antipodal generators; nine 12-point cyclic-shift-plus-antipode orbits plus four antipodal pairs; and signed-permutation/lattice-pattern orbits generated from a few parameterized vectors such as permutations of $(a,a,b,0,0,0)$ and $(a,a,a,b,b,0)$ with incomplete orbits selected to total 116. For each family, use at least 20 random generator seeds, optimize only the generators with Adam on an annealed soft-max objective ($T$ from $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-4}$), expand to the full code for scoring, and then gradually release the symmetry by blending the symmetric gradient with the free gradient before a final unconstrained quench and capped LP polish. Keep the best released code found, but always retain the loaded incumbent as a safe return value if no symmetric basin beats it.

idea: Antipodal plus signed-permutation orbit search with Riemannian Adam then symmetry-breaking release and re-jam.
direction: Search explicitly for the missing symmetric/antipodal structure in reduced coordinates: parametrise 58 antipodal pairs by $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{58\times6}$ with $X=[Y;-Y]$, optimise $Y$ with Riemannian Adam on the softmax objective ($\beta:30\to300$, lr $0.01\to0.001$, 1500 steps, several seeds including seeds derived from signed-permutation/cyclic orbits of a few generic generators under the group generated by coordinate 6-cycles and even sign flips), then do a symmetry-breaking release — add tangent noise of sizes $10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2}$ to break the antipodality, requench unconstrained, and LP-polish. Also test a purely orbit-based variant where only the generator seeds (orbit sizes summing to 116) are variables. Accept a symmetric candidate for polishing if it reaches below 0.605 constrained, since a near-optimal symmetric basin released and re-jammed is exactly the structural alternative to the current amorphous jam; cap this at 120s and fall back to the incumbent on any failure.

idea: De-novo N-homotopy from random and D6-shell seeds at N=96/104/112 grown by deepest-hole insertion and from N=124 pruned by contact-load deletion with annealed softmax-Adam requenches, diverse-pool filtering, and single final LP polish.
direction: $N$-homotopy built de novo, never starting from the record: build codes for $N=96,104,112$ from scratch with annealed softmax Adam (multiple random seeds plus D6-lattice-shell seeds), then grow to 116 by repeatedly inserting the deepest-hole point (max inner product minimised over 20k random candidates plus local refinement) and re-quenching after each insertion; in parallel run the reverse path, optimise $N=124$, then prune one point at a time — always the point with the largest contact count weighted by pair tightness — re-quenching briefly after each deletion down to 116. Maintain a small diverse pool (reject pool members whose sorted Gram spectrum is within $10^{-6}$ of an existing member), LP-polish only the best structurally distinct end-point for the final 20s, enforce a hard internal deadline of 150s with time checks every 32 iterations, and return the best of pool/incumbent.

idea: Antipodal 58-pair plus few-generator orbit search with Riemannian Adam then symmetry-breaking release and requench plus LP re-jam.
direction: Search explicitly for the missing symmetric/antipodal structure in reduced coordinates: parametrise 58 antipodal pairs by $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{58\times6}$ with $X=[Y;-Y]$, optimise $Y$ with Riemannian Adam on the softmax objective ($\beta:30\to300$, lr $0.01\to0.001$, 1500 steps, several seeds including seeds derived from signed-permutation/cyclic orbits of a few generic generators under the group generated by coordinate 6-cycles and even sign flips), then do a symmetry-breaking release — add tangent noise of sizes $10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2}$ to break the antipodality, requench unconstrained, and LP-polish. Also test a purely orbit-based variant where only the generator seeds (orbit sizes summing to 116) are variables. Accept a symmetric candidate for polishing if it reaches below 0.605 constrained, since a near-optimal symmetric basin released and re-jammed is exactly the structural alternative to the current amorphous jam; cap this at 120s and fall back to the incumbent on any failure.

idea: De-novo N-homotopy without the record — quench small random/D6 codes then grow by deepest-hole insertion and shrink from N=124 by contact-weighted pruning, keeping a spectrum-diverse pool.
direction: $N$-homotopy built de novo, never starting from the record: build codes for $N=96,104,112$ from scratch with annealed softmax Adam (multiple random seeds plus D6-lattice-shell seeds), then grow to 116 by repeatedly inserting the deepest-hole point (max inner product minimised over 20k random candidates plus local refinement) and re-quenching after each insertion; in parallel run the reverse path, optimise $N=124$, then prune one point at a time — always the point with the largest contact count weighted by pair tightness — re-quenching briefly after each deletion down to 116. Maintain a small diverse pool (reject pool members whose sorted Gram spectrum is within $10^{-6}$ of an existing member), LP-polish only the best structurally distinct end-point for the final 20s, enforce a hard internal deadline of 150s with time checks every 32 iterations, and return the best of pool/incumbent.

idea: Hub-deletion deep-hole surgery with frozen-hinge plus annealed-softmax reconvergence and topology-gated LP re-jamming.
direction: Targeted contact-graph surgery on the overloaded hubs: from the incumbent, programmatically find points with $\ge$14 contacts (the hubs creating the jam) and, in separate trials, delete 3, 5, or 8 of them plus optionally 1–2 points with $\le$3 contacts, then refill by deep-hole insertion — sample $\ge$50k random unit vectors against the kept core, take the candidate minimising the maximum inner product, refine it by 50 steps of repulsion from its current argmax neighbour, insert greedily one at a time. Re-optimise in two stages (first only the inserted points with the core frozen for 200 hinge steps at band 0.01, then all points with a 300-step annealed softmax, $T:0.02\to0.002$), screen cheaply and LP-polish only candidates already below 0.598, cycle this until $t=140$s with the incumbent stored as an always-returnable fallback, and keep a candidate only if its contact graph differs from the incumbent's (e.g. $\ge$5% edge change), not merely if its score ties.

idea: Nullspace escape from the jammed basin via SVD of the active-pair Jacobian with rotation removal and second-shell line search plus hinge/LP re-jamming.
direction: A deliberately small, robust second-order escape along the contact nullspace: compute the $\sim$540 active pairs (slack $<10^{-9}$), build their Jacobian in tangent coordinates ($540\times580$, using a per-point orthonormal tangent basis from one SVD per point), take its SVD once with dense numpy to get the $\approx$25-dimensional nullspace, and sample random nullspace directions (plus directions aligned with the lowest right-singular vectors); for each, do an exact line search over step sizes $\pm\{10^{-4}\dots3\times10^{-2}\}$ scoring the true maximum including the next shell of pairs (ranks 540–750, slack up to $10^{-4}$), keep moves that reduce the second-shell pressure (e.g. the 600th largest cosine) without raising the maximum, then re-jam with a short hinge quench and a single trust-region LP. This exploits the fact that first-order LP is exhausted but curvature through the near-nullspace is not; implement it with numpy only, no repeated sparse LP in a loop, a 150s deadline, and immediate fallback to the incumbent if any linear algebra fails.
